gap: A system clock set before 1970 is not handled in the ordering the oracle rows depend on.
why it is not covered: No oracle row runs with a pre-epoch clock (review finding P4, noted as a residual).

gap: The stored-read path has no routing-profile twin row.
why it is not covered: The task fixture's post and get carry no session id, so a session-bound profile cannot be exercised on a stored read without a fixture change of more than 30 lines.

gap: The stored-read path has no key-scope twin row.
why it is not covered: A key scoped away from the tool cannot create the task, so no stored read of it can exist; the live key-scope rows cover the refusal.

gap: A playbook step keeps the strict step refusal, not the missing-name answer.
why it is not covered: By design: a step is operator-defined, so its refusal names the definition, not a caller-chosen name.

gap: On /mcp/{backend}, a caller with no view of a managed backend gets -32601 for a policy-withheld name but the account's connect answer for a missing one (ruling B on the direct route).
why it is not covered: Open, not a residual: the fix needs a crate-visible entry to the side-effect-free no-view predicate, an operator visibility decision. Its red row is parked off the branch.

gap: A resumed keyed chain whose next step is a missing name mints that step's credential before failing at dispatch; a withheld step is refused before its fingerprint resolves a credential.
why it is not covered: The order of work differs (a credential is minted for the missing name), but the caller's answer is the same for both; no row measures the mint.

gap: Under Standard with a truncated or unread tool list, and under input_schema_enforcement Off, a missing name is forwarded to the backend while a hidden one is answered by the gateway.
why it is not covered: The gateway cannot tell a missing name from an undeclared one without a complete list; Off is the operator's choice to forward. Rows S5, S6 and S3b pin the forward.
